title: chiron linguistic-substrate datamodel
purpose: Machine-readable description of the ideal underlying data model of the chiron linguistic substrate, for consumption by a design agent optimizing typography and building a theming system. Every attribute carries a contentKind so type decisions can be made from what the text IS (prose, headword, identifier, verbatim quote, numeral) rather than from any current CSS.

authority.capsMirror: tools/lingua/dimensions/{lexicon,phrasebook,relations}.py validate_payload — each methodology doc's 'Schema and caps' section mirrors its dimension's validator by project contract
authority.note: This file follows the methodology (the theory), NOT the current web viewer's types. The as-built UI is described separately in design/ui-map.json; the two are intentionally different views.

contentKinds.prose: Running text meant to be read: definitions, glosses, intents, descriptions. Wants a comfortable reading measure and line height.
contentKinds.headword: The canonical display form of a named thing (term, phrase, title). Set as an entry heading; the corpus's spelling wins, even when unusual.
contentKinds.label: Short UI-facing name for a container or category (group label, dimension label, kind badge). Scannable, often uppercase/tracked in chrome.
contentKinds.identifier: Machine-facing slug, id, hash, or path. Monospace-leaning; must never wrap mid-token; lowercase-kebab by law.
contentKinds.code: Text meant to be pasted into a prompt or terminal, or read as source (templates with {slots}, commands). Monospace block.
contentKinds.quote: Verbatim source material, mechanically verified against the corpus. Must visually read as evidence — distinct from any paraphrase or callout.
contentKinds.count: Numeral (totals, chapter numbers, cardinalities). Wants tabular figures.

vocabulary.corpus: Any git repo or folder mounted as learning material — a documented course or an undocumented codebase. The unit that HAS a working language. Deliberately not 'course'.
vocabulary.register: One retelling of the same material under its own translation requirements (v1, v2, …). The linguistics sense: a variety of language for a setting. Two registers are two ways of speaking about one source, not two revisions. Deliberately not 'iteration' or 'version'.
vocabulary.group: An ordered section within a corpus. Deliberately not 'tier', 'module', or 'section'.
vocabulary.chapter: One coherent unit of material — a document, or a coherent code unit. The unit of anchoring, of authoring, and of drift. Deliberately not 'lesson'.
vocabulary.dimension: One orthogonal projection of the corpus's working language. dimension = mode slug = methodology doc = dimension module: the same string names all of them.
vocabulary.mode: A slug a register elects in translation.yaml. 'implemented' modes have machinery; 'recorded' modes have only a written methodology — the entry path for new dimensions.
vocabulary.substrate: The extracted linguistic data as a whole. Explicitly not a summary: it answers 'what is this called here', 'how do I say it', 'how do the names relate'.
vocabulary.grounding: Every claim traceable to a verbatim quote in the material, enforced by tooling. If the chapter doesn't say it, it does not go in; where the chapter and outside knowledge disagree, the chapter wins.
vocabulary.anchor: The grounding primitive: a verbatim quote from a chapter, pinned to the content hash the quote was authored against.
vocabulary.drift: Two linked senses. Instructional drift: generic phrasing forces an agent to guess the mapping. Substrate drift: source content changing under an anchor, so its pin no longer matches — detected per anchor, never per corpus.
vocabulary.define-vs-mention: A term is DEFINED in exactly one chapter (defined_in) and MENTIONED everywhere else it is anchored. Writes declare which: define:true upserts the full entry; define:false contributes anchors only.
vocabulary.translation: The extraction act — retelling the corpus into the substrate under the register's recorded requirements.
vocabulary.calibration: The learner's activity: adjusting their own language against the substrate until instructions transfer without lookup.
vocabulary.entry: One addressable unit of the substrate — one term, one phrasing, or one relation edge — regardless of dimension. What `./ch ask` returns, what `./ch grade` matches against, and what the viewer's lookup modal renders. Deliberately not 'bit', which was minted in the retrieval/viewer layer and never ratified in methodology/, README's vocabulary table, or this file; entries are never addressed by a URL of their own.

corpus.description: Mounted material with a working language. Owns one source/ checkout shared by all registers.

name.notes: Directory id under devenv/reference/; must not look like a register (vN).

checkout.notes: Git short SHA of source/, or 'unknown' for non-repos.

origin.notes: Where the corpus was mounted from.

registers.notes: Each register is an independent retelling; re-mounting creates the next one.

source.notes: devenv/reference/<name>/source/ — read-only material shared by ALL registers.

register.description: One retelling of the corpus under its own translation requirements. Owns its data/*.yaml (one file per implemented dimension), pages/, and adapter. A HARD BOUNDARY: nothing in a register's data references another register — every cross-reference is a register-local id.

name.notes: v1, v2, … Registers are retellings, not versions.

label.notes: One-line description of this retelling, e.g. 'essays + 2025-05 workshop'.

modes.notes: The dimensions this register elects. An unselected mode is not tracked at all — no data file, no state, no coverage pressure.

notes.notes: Free text steering the authoring agents.

modes.notes: Each mode resolves to an implemented dimension or stays recorded.

terms.notes: The lexicon: data/lexicon.yaml, keyed by slug.

phrases.notes: The phrasebook: data/phrasebook.yaml, keyed by slug.

edges.notes: Concept relations: data/relations.yaml, a flat edge list.

group.description: An ordered section within a corpus's chapters.

id.notes: Reserved ids rejected at scan (they would shadow viewer routes): lexicon, phrasebook, relations, concept-relations, chat, api, assets.

chapter.description: One coherent unit of material: a single document (kind=doc) or a coherent code unit (kind=code). THE unit of anchoring, authoring, and drift. Two id forms exist: the global id '<corpus>/<vN>/<group>/<NN>' and the register-local id '<group>/<NN>' — anchors and defined_in always use the local form.

number.notes: Ordering token within the group: '01', '02b'. Displayed as a numeral; wants tabular figures.

kind.notes: Changes validation: anchors into a code chapter must name a path.

unit_paths.notes: Ordered files constituting the chapter — a doc chapter has exactly one, a code chapter all included files. Anchor quotes are verified against exactly these files.

primary_path.notes: The unit's entry point (the doc itself, or README/__init__/entry file).

content_hash.notes: The drift pin. Computed from COMMITTED git blobs, not the working tree, so local edits never falsely flag drift.

defines.notes: Inverse of term.defined_in — exactly one chapter owns each term's definition.

anchors.notes: Every anchor names exactly one chapter (its local id); a chapter that changes marks exactly its own anchors stale.

dimension.description: One orthogonal projection of the working language. First-class and closed: each is one mode slug + one methodology doc + one implementation module, all named by the same string. Registry order is semantic, not cosmetic — lexicon comes first because the other two reference its slugs; authoring and display both follow it.

dataFilename.notes: Explicit because it is the one divergence from 'the three names are the same string': concept-relations stores relations.yaml.

noun.notes: How the dimension describes itself in a sentence.

countNoun.notes: The word used with totals: '131 terms'.

instances.label: Phrasebook
instances.answers: How do I say it when instructing an agent?

mode.description: A register's election of a dimension slug in translation.yaml. An OPEN set: any slug matching the pattern may be recorded; the closed subset with machinery is the dimension registry. A recorded mode (methodology written, no implementation) is how a new dimension enters the system — write the plan first, ship the machinery when it earns it.

status.notes: implemented ⟺ slug in the dimension registry. Recorded modes are surfaced (badged) but nothing renders their data — there is none.

term.description: One thing the corpus names: the canonical surface form, what kind of name it is, a definition in the corpus's own words, and anchors proving the corpus really says this. The definition is deliberately short — the lexicon teaches NAMING, not the material itself. Register-scoped entity (one entry per concept however many chapters touch it); chapter-scoped writes — mirroring how vocabulary lives in a repository: defined once, used everywhere.

slug.notes: Reused, never re-minted: the slug index exists so authors reuse slugs instead of forking them.

term.notes: The corpus's spelling wins, even when it is unusual.

kind.notes: What kind of name this is. Rendered as a badge next to the headword.

definition.notes: In the corpus's own words; keeps concrete details that make the term usable in a prompt (signatures, defaults, file locations).

aliases.notes: Competing spellings the corpus also uses.

defined_in.notes: Exactly one owning chapter. Stamped by the writer from define:true payloads — never authored directly.

anchors.notes: Across ALL chapters that define or mention the term.

definedIn.notes: One definition per term per register; cross-chapter redefinition is human-gated.

mentionedIn.notes: Derived: every chapter appearing in anchors other than defined_in.

edges.notes: As from- or to-endpoint; direction is semantic.

phrase.description: One canonical phrasing — a fixed way the corpus combines its names. The verb tells the agent which operation, the preposition which relationship. No ownership concept: content is last-writer-wins; the validator loop polices quality.

phrase.notes: The collocation as the corpus uses it.

intent.notes: When a learner reaches for this phrasing.

template.notes: An instruction with {slots} the learner fills — something to paste into a prompt. Slots are unparsed free text.

terms.notes: Every slug must already exist: lexicon before phrasebook.
A dangling reference (term later removed) is a warning, not drift — deliberately weaker than the edge rule.

relationEdge.description: One typed, directed edge between two lexicon terms, with a one-line gloss and anchors proving the corpus asserts the link. Names alone are a bag of words; relations are what make multi-step instructions coherent — you can only say 'wire X into Y' correctly if you know X feeds Y and not the reverse. Edges have no slug: identity is the composite (from, type, to), so parallel edges of different types between the same pair are legal.

from.notes: The actor/source. Must exist in the lexicon.

to.notes: The target. Must exist and differ from 'from' — no self-loops.

type.notes: Closed by design so viewer and learning agent can rely on edge semantics; extending it is a deliberate change (one line of code plus the methodology doc), not a per-entry choice.

gloss.notes: Written to read left-to-right along the edge direction.

anchors.notes: A second chapter anchoring the same edge merges its anchors in; gloss is last-writer-wins.

anchoredIn.notes: Via anchors. An edge whose endpoint vanishes from the lexicon marks its anchoring chapters stale — dangling is drift even when hashes match.

anchor.description: The grounding primitive, a value object owned by its entry (term, phrase, or edge). Grounding is enforced by tooling, not good intentions: the quote must be found verbatim (after whitespace normalization) in the anchored chapter's own files, and is pinned to the content hash the chapter had when authored.
identity: (owned by entry; keyed by chapter for drop/merge)

chapter.notes: '<group>/<NN>' — an anchor may only name its own target chapter.

path.notes: Source-relative; must be one of the chapter's unit_paths.

quote.notes: Verbatim. The ONLY verbatim-source content in the whole substrate — typographically this is evidence, distinct from every paraphrase.

curated_against.notes: The drift pin, stamped by the writer — authors never handle hashes. Stale ⟺ pin no longer equals the chapter's content_hash.

state.description: Extraction state per (chapter, dimension). DERIVED, never stored — computed from the anchors referencing that chapter plus dimension-specific drift rules. Register-level state is worst-of-chapters.

calibrationEvent.description: One graded utterance by the learner, appended by `./ch grade`. The record of the activity this file already names calibration, which until now had machinery in neither surface. Deliberately NOT substrate: it lives under work/, never enters the manifest, is never read by web/, and losing it costs nothing.

ts.notes: UTC, second resolution. Append-only: no update, no delete.

hits.notes: Entry ids the utterance landed on.

misses.notes: Drift runs — each one a place an agent must guess.

verdict.notes: lands | drifts | hit | miss — the CLI's exit code, never a model's opinion.

relationships.references: term/phrase/relationEdge by entry id, with no referential integrity: entries may be re-authored underneath it

dimensionState.notes: ok = anchors present, all pins current; stale = some pin diverges from the chapter's content_hash (or, for concept-relations, a dangling endpoint); none = nothing anchored here. Aggregation order: stale > none > ok.

termKind.notes: What kind of name a term is. A flat enum with no sub-structure — concrete details (signatures, defaults, locations) fold into the definition prose.

values.feeds: output of one becomes input of the other
values.configures: one thing sets the other's behavior
values.contrasts-with: the corpus explicitly distinguishes the two
values.implements: a concrete thing realizes a contract/idea

relationType.notes: Closed by design. Direction is semantic: from = actor/source, to = target.

chapterKind.notes: kind=code tightens anchor validation: path becomes required.

perPayload.note: A payload is the authoring unit: one JSON document for one (dimension, chapter) pair.

invariants.law: Every entry carries 1–8 anchors; an entry with zero anchors does not exist (entries losing their last anchor are deleted on write).
Anchor quotes are verbatim and mechanically verified against the chapter's own files; whitespace normalization is the only permitted deviation.
Drift is per-anchor, not per-entry and not per-corpus: a term anchored in three chapters goes stale only where content changed. Pins track committed content, not the working tree.
State is derived, never stored; register state is worst-of-chapters (stale > none > ok).
One definition per term per register: exactly one chapter is defined_in; all others contribute mention anchors.
Cross-chapter redefinition is rejected without an explicit human-gated flag; undeclared define-conflicts auto-demote to mentions, with the earlier chapter in register order winning.
Slugs are reused, never re-minted: mention-only writes (define:false) on an unknown slug are violations; the slug index keeps authors converging on one slug per concept.
Lexicon before phrasebook and before relations: dependent payloads referencing missing term slugs are validation errors, and registry order encodes it.
Edge identity is (from, type, to): duplicates within a payload are rejected; a second chapter anchoring the same edge merges anchors in (gloss last-writer-wins). No self-loops.
A dangling edge endpoint is drift even when hashes match; a dangling phrase→term reference is only a warning. The asymmetry is deliberate.
Writes are chapter-scoped drop-then-apply: a set for chapter C first drops all of C's existing anchors, then applies the payload — making re-authoring idempotent and removals possible.
Content is last-writer-wins for phrases and glosses but ownership-gated for definitions — the one deliberate asymmetry between dimensions.
An unselected mode is not tracked at all — no data file, no state, no coverage pressure; an implemented but unelected mode cannot be written to.
The register is a hard reference boundary: defined_in and every anchor use register-local chapter ids; nothing in data/ can point across registers.
Authors never handle hashes: curated_against is stamped by the writer, and grounding failures are rejections, not warnings.
dimension = mode slug = methodology doc = dimension module; the methodology is executed, not merely cited (its procedure/schema/quality sections are embedded verbatim in every extract bundle).
Reserved group ids (lexicon, phrasebook, relations, concept-relations, chat, api, assets) are rejected at scan — they would shadow viewer routes.

modelingNotes: Quote single-line is enforced by the validator but stated in no methodology 'Schema and caps' section.
term.definition and phrase.template are the only multi-line fields; the docs state this for template but not for definition.
Only the lexicon has a per-file cap (500); phrasebook and relations have none — an open asymmetry.

The 'three names are the same string' law holds for slug/mode/methodology-doc; the data filename diverges once (concept-relations → relations.yaml), which is why dataFilename is an explicit dimension attribute.
Edges have no stable identity beyond (from, type, to): renaming a term slug silently destroys every edge referencing it; terms have slugs, edges do not.
All cross-references are register-relative; 'the same term across v1 and v2' has no representation at all.
aliases are stored but never indexed or surfaced as lookup keys, despite the methodology asking authors to record competing spellings for exactly that purpose.
template {slots} are unparsed free text — no slot list, no types, no linkage from slot names to lexicon slugs, despite template being the one artifact meant to be pasted into a real prompt.

`bit` (chroma.py, web/lib/navigator-types.ts, /api/bit) is the viewer layer's unratified name for what the methodology calls an entry — the word is retired in prose and new code, but the web/ rename and the chroma collection rename are deferred because both touch persisted state.
No fourth dimension is designed anywhere; the extension point is fully specified (recorded modes) but empty. Treat mode as an open slug set and dimension as the closed implemented subset.
